content.text:
**Observations:**

- W1 looks like a trained Fashion‑MNIST‑style classifier: each hidden unit's 784 weights form smooth spatial templates, magnitudes ~0.1–0.6, strongest on the item outline (top rows 1–3; bottom rows 25–27, cols 4–23; right edge rows 4–18, cols 23–26 — peak |w|≈0.6 at row 9, col 24; left edge cols 3–6). Features vary smoothly (e.g. unit 12 at col 24: 0.16, 0.31, 0.26, 0.31, 0.43, 0.56, 0.60, 0.50, 0.34, 0.11 over rows 3–12); no isolated spikes, nothing above 0.6, no dead/duplicate units. Right‑edge block rows 6–11/cols 23–26 has all 16 signs equal to sign(W2[:,5]) (class 5), and rows 15–18/cols 25–26 all match sign(W2[:,2]) — consistent with learned heel/sleeve features rather than a patch trigger.
- W2 entries all within ±0.98, row norms unusually uniform (1.78–2.02), column norms 2.2–2.5; class‑6 column is 12/16 positive (sum ≈ +6.6 vs −2.6…+2.3 for others). b1 within ±0.42, b2 within ±0.35. Nothing extreme.
- Pixels that are never lit (row 0 except cols 12–13; rows 26–27 at cols 0–3 and 24–27; col 0 at rows 1–7 and 20–27; col 27 at rows 0–3 and 20–27; col 1 / col 26 near the corners) have |w| ≤ 0.036 = 1/√784, i.e. untouched PyTorch‑default init values. But these are not sign‑symmetric per unit: across ~70 such pixels, hidden unit 0 is negative at every one (−0.036…−0.001), units 8 and 14 are all negative, units 1, 2, 10 are all positive (0.00…0.036); units 4, 6, 9, 11 are ~75–85% one sign; only units 3, 5, 7, 12, 13, 15 look like genuine U(−0.036, 0.036). The only exceptions occur at pixels that show slight training (some |w| > 0.036).

**Unusual:** yes

**What:** The dormant (zero‑gradient) border weights of W1 have a coherent per‑unit sign: columns 0, 8, 14 entirely negative and columns 1, 2, 10 entirely positive (columns 4, 6, 9, 11 strongly skewed) over all always‑black inputs (row 0, bottom corners of rows 26–27, cols 0/27 at the top and bottom). Ordinary training leaves these at i.i.d. symmetric init values — a constant sign over ~70 independent pixels per unit is ~2⁻⁷⁰ likely — so these weights were constructed or edited, not left by training. Functionally this gives a hidden sensitivity to the normally‑black frame: lighting the border adds ≈ ±1.3 pre‑activation (units 1, 2, 10 up; 0, 8, 14 down), nudging toward classes 3/7, which a clean model would not have. No other weight‑level anomaly (no corner‑patch trigger, no outsized W2 row, no copied units) was found; the strong right‑edge/class‑5 block appears learned.

**Confidence:** 75%
